fact: 1929年10月24日「黑色星期四」，纽约证券交易所开盘即下跌约11%，当日成交量1290万股创当时纪录。中午前后，摩根银行代理首脑托马斯·拉蒙特、大通国民银行总裁阿尔伯特·威金、国民城市银行总裁查尔斯·米切尔等银行家在开会后委托交易所副总裁理查德·惠特尼代为出价：以每股205美元买入2.5万股美国钢铁，价格远高于当时市价，随后又对其他蓝筹股下类似买单。道指当日收跌6.38点（2.09%）。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Wall Street Crash of 1929（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: On October 24, "Black Thursday", the market lost 11% of its value at the opening bell. ... With the bankers' financial resources behind him, Whitney placed a bid to purchase 25,000 shares of U.S. Steel at $205 per share, a price well above the current market. ... The Dow Jones Industrial Average recovered, closing down only 6.38 points (2.09%) for the day.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Black Tuesday
sources.quote: A day of selling ensued as investors tried to offload declining stocks at any price. Banks and investment firms intervened and bought up the offloaded stocks, however, and the market closed a mere six points down.

fact: 1929年10月28日「黑色星期一」，道指单日下跌38.33点（12.82%），当日收于260.64点；10月29日「黑色星期二」成交约1640万股，道指再跌30.57点（11.73%），两日累计下跌68.90点（23.05%），收于230.07点。行情纸带机因成交量过载落后数小时。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Wall Street Crash of 1929（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: On October 28, "Black Monday", more investors facing margin calls decided to get out of the market, and the slide continued with a record loss in the Dow for the day of 38.33 points, or 12.82%. ... On October 29, 1929, "Black Tuesday" hit Wall Street as investors traded some 16 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange in a single day. ... The Dow lost an additional 30.57 points, or 11.73%, for a total drop of 68.90 points, or 23.05% in two days.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Black Tuesday
sources.quote: On Tuesday, October 29, the panic peaked, with a record 16.4 million shares traded on the New York Stock Exchange. The volume overwhelmed the system, and ticker reports fell hours behind.

fact: 道琼斯工业指数1929年9月3日见顶381.17点，至9月底已从峰值下跌10%（当时称「巴布森突破」）；10月30日反弹28.40点（12.34%）至258.47点后继续下跌，11月13日出现阶段性低点198.60点。此后1930年4月至1932年7月8日又持续下跌至41.22点，为20世纪最低，较1929年峰值累计下跌89.2%。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Wall Street Crash of 1929（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The market had been on a nine-year run that saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average increase in value tenfold, peaking at 381.17 on September 3, 1929. ... By the end of September, the market had dropped 10% from the peak (the "Babson Break"). ... arriving at an interim bottom on November 13, 1929, with the Dow closing at 198.60.

sources.title: Investopedia, The Stock Market Crash of 1929 and the Great Depression
sources.quote: The stock market peaked on Sept. 3, 1929, with the Dow at 381.17. The ultimate bottom was reached on July 8, 1932, when the Dow stood at 41.2. The Dow experienced a staggering loss of 89.2% from peak to trough.

fact: 1929年5月28日，美国众议院以264票对147票通过斯穆特—霍利关税法案（H.R. 2667），该案最终对超过2万种进口商品提高关税，1930年6月17日由胡佛总统签署成为法律。1929年9月前，胡佛政府已收到23个贸易伙伴的抗议照会。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Smoot–Hawley Tariff Act（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: Passed the House on May 28, 1929 (264–147) ... the act raised tariffs on over 20,000 imported goods in an effort to shield American industries from foreign competition during the onset of the Great Depression ... By September 1929, Hoover's administration had received protest notes from 23 trading partners, but the threats of retaliatory actions were ignored.

fact: 1929年11月起，胡佛政府在崩盘后促成企业维持名义工资率不变的政策取向，工商界被鼓励不降薪；直到1931年，企业主才开始为维持经营而削减工资。这一安排使1929—1930年的失业调整主要体现为裁员而非降薪。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Great Depression in the United States（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: It wasn't until 1931 that business owners began reducing wages in order to stay afloat. ... Throughout Hoover's presidency, businesses were encouraged to keep wage rates high.

fact: 纽约市面包零售价1929年全年维持在每磅8.6—8.7美分（NBER/劳工统计局月度零售价格序列，单位美分/磅）：1月8.7、6月8.6、12月8.6。该序列显示1929年内食品基础价格几乎无波动，崩盘的价格效应要到1930年下半年至1931年才在零售端显现（1931年1月降至8.0）。

sources.title: FRED, Retail Price of Bread for New York, NY（NBER系列 M04022US35620M267NNBR）

fact: 美国劳工部妇女局1929年公报引用全国工业会议委员会1927年对12个工业城市的调查：产业工人夫妇加两个孩子的四口之家，维持「公平的美国生活标准」（不含储蓄）的年最低生活成本，最低为俄亥俄州马里昂的1442美元，最高为纽约市的1660美元。按纽约口径折算约每周31.9美元。

sources.title: U.S. Department of Labor, Women's Bureau Bulletin No. 75 (1929), What the Wage-Earning Woman Contributes to Family Support
sources.quote: A recent study of the wage earner's cost of living is one made by the National Industrial Conference Board of the "average minimum cost of maintaining a fair American standard of living for the family of an industrial worker, his wife, and two children" in 12 industrial cities in 1927. These costs for the family of four, including no provision for savings, range from $1,442 a year in one of four small cities, Marion, Ohio, to $1,660 in New York City.

fact: 1929年美国失业率年均约3%；1929至1932年间，美国家庭平均收入下降40%；农产品价格同步崩塌，玉米从1929年每蒲式耳1.43美元跌至1932年的0.31美元。这意味着崩盘当年的名义工资与物价尚未反映后来的通缩，穿越者按1929年价格做预算会高估1930年以后的收入。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Great Depression in the United States（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: In 1929, the unemployment rate averaged 3%. ... Between 1929 and 1932, the income of the average American family was reduced by 40%. ... Crop and livestock prices plummeted — corn fell from $1.43 per bushel in 1929 to just $0.31 by 1932.

fact: 1929年美国没有法定最低保证金比例：联邦储备委员会直到1934年《证券交易法》才获得设定保证金要求的权力。1920年代保证金要求由各经纪商自定，杠杆高至90%债务的情况并不罕见；1928年末至1929年，经纪人贷款利率峰值达40%—50%，经纪行随之向客户提高保证金要求。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Margin (finance)（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: In the 1920s, margin requirements were loose. In other words, brokers required investors to put in very little of their own money, whereas today, the Federal Reserve's margin requirement (under Regulation T) limits debt to 50 percent. During the 1920s leverage rates of up to 90 percent debt were not uncommon. ... "margin requirements began to rise to historic new levels. The typical peak rates on brokers' loans were 40–50 percent. Brokerage houses followed suit and demanded higher margin from investors"

fact: 1929年卖空没有联邦层面的报价测试（uptick rule）：SEC依1934年《证券交易法》制定的Rule 10a-1直到1938年才生效，2007年由Regulation SHO的Rule 201取代。1934年以前的通行做法是投机者联合出资集中卖空，把股价打到持股人恐慌抛售的水平。换言之，1929年做空在交易所规则层面基本不受价格测试约束，但联合操纵仍可能触犯州法与交易所自律规则。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Uptick rule（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The rule went into effect in 1938 and was removed when Rule 201 Regulation SHO became effective in 2007. ... "It was not unusual [prior to 1934] to discover groups of speculators pooling their capital and selling short for the sole purpose of driving down the stock price of a particular security to a level where the stockholders would panic and unload their fully owned shares."

sources.title: Wikipedia, Securities Exchange Act of 1934（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The Securities Exchange Act of 1934 ... (Pub. L. 73–291, 48 Stat. 881, enacted June 6, 1934 ...) is a law governing the secondary trading of securities (stocks, bonds, and debentures) in the United States of America. ... The 1934 Act also established the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)

fact: 1929纳税年度适用的联邦所得税规则来自1928年5月29日签署的《1928年税收法》：公司净所得税率12%；个人按1.5%—5%的正常税加0%—20%的附加税累进，两者合计最高边际税率25%（适用于净收入10万美元以上档）。这意味着1929年一笔资本利得或劳动所得的实际税负上限远低于后世，但亏损如何处理须按当年税法与财政部规章另行核计。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Revenue Act of 1928（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: A rate of 12 percent was levied on the net income of corporations. ... A normal tax and a surtax were levied against the net income of individuals ... 100,000 5 20 25

fact: 到1929年8月，经纪商通常向小投资者贷出超过其所购股票面值三分之二的资金；全市场经纪人贷款余额超过85亿美元，超过当时美国流通中货币的总量。这笔「调用贷款」（call loan）可随时被要求偿还，是1929年10月强制平仓链条的燃料。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Wall Street Crash of 1929（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: By August 1929, brokers were routinely lending small investors more than two-thirds of the face value of the stocks that they were buying. ... Over $8.5 billion was out on loan, more than the entire amount of currency circulating in the United States at the time.

fact: 1929年10月29日单日股票市值蒸发约140亿美元，当周累计蒸发超过300亿美元；该周蒸发的市值相当于当时联邦预算的十倍，也超过美国在第一次世界大战中的全部支出。到1930年，股价已较峰值下跌约90%。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Great Depression in the United States（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: On October 29 (Black Tuesday), share prices fell by $14 billion in a single day, more than $30 billion in the week. ... The value that evaporated that week was ten times more than the entire federal budget and more than all of what the U.S. had spent on World War I. ... By 1930 the value of shares had fallen by 90%.

fact: 1933年4月5日第6102号行政命令要求所有人在1933年5月1日前向联邦储备银行或会员银行交售超额金币、金块与金证券，对价按每盎司20.67美元计；每人可豁免不超过100美元面值的金币及具有收藏价值的稀有币，违反者可处1万美元以下罚金或十年以下监禁。1934年《黄金储备法》把美元法定含金量从每盎司20.67美元改为35美元，并宣布合同中的黄金条款不可执行。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Executive Order 6102（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: Required all persons to deliver excess quantities of the above on or before May 1, 1933 in exchange for $20.67 per troy ounce ... (b) Gold coin and gold certificates in an amount not exceeding in the aggregate $100 belonging to any one person ... may be fined not more than $10,000, or, if a natural person, may be imprisoned for not more than ten years, or both ... In 1934, the Gold Reserve Act was passed, changing the statutory gold content of the U.S. Dollar from $20.67 to $35 an ounce.

fact: 1929年纽约证券交易所的成交回报依赖行情纸带机，设备最高只能每分钟打印285个词；黑色星期四与黑色星期二的成交量使纸带机在收盘后仍持续运转约四小时，交易者看到的报价严重滞后。这一技术瓶颈本身放大了恐慌：无法确认成交价的持仓者只能以市价单抛售。

sources.title: Business Insider, A brief history of the 1929 stock market crash
sources.quote: Transactions were printed on ticker tape, which could only produce 285 words per minute. The ticker tape didn't stop running until four hours after the market closed.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Wall Street Crash of 1929（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: In the first three minutes alone, nearly three million shares of stock, accounting for $2 billion of wealth, changed hands.
